name: web-stage3-packaging-budgets
title: Web build stage 3: precompressed outputs, size manifest and enforced size budgets in CI, lazy asset pack option, profiles built in CI, MIME-fallback loader (issue #155, stage 3)
issue: Issue #155 stage 3 (read the issue body with `bash "C:/Method Notes Obsidian/gh-epicnicks.sh" api repos/EpicNicks/N2Engine/issues/155 --jq .body` from inside the repo) and the merged stages 0-2 (docs/web-build.html, cmake/N2EngineWeb.cmake, the web player package from stage 2, the stage 0 size-report script and web-size-report target, the web CI job). Decisions already taken (do NOT revisit): static files only, ANY host, NO special headers (no cross-origin isolation), relative URLs, MIME/compression-agnostic output, profiles dev/size/speed architected from the start, size budgets enforced in CI. SCOPE OF STAGE 3 (assets and packaging): (1) PRECOMPRESSED outputs: in the `size`/`speed` profile packages produce `.br` and `.gz` siblings of the wasm/js/data files (brotli/gzip via the toolchain or Python stdlib gzip + a pinned `brotli` Python module OR the `brotli` CLI if available in the emsdk/runner: pick what is robust and pinned) AND the plain files remain (the output must work on a host that does neither); document how to serve them (e.g. nginx/Apache/Netlify snippets for Content-Encoding) and that nothing is required; (2) a SIZE MANIFEST: a generated `manifest.json` in the package (file names, raw size, gzip size, brotli size, sha256) used by the loader for cache busting and by CI for budgets; (3) ENFORCED BUDGETS in CI: set concrete initial budgets (derive them from the measured sizes of the current stage 2 package with sensible headroom: measure in the CI job summary first by reading the job logs of recent web jobs; record the chosen numbers and reasoning in docs and the PR; budgets live in one place (a JSON/CMake file) and the script fails the web job when exceeded); (4) build the `size` and `speed` profiles in CI too (stage 0 only configured them): the size profile must build the player package; keep the CI time reasonable (state the added minutes; consider building size only on one job leg, but you may only add steps to the existing web job or one new job whose name you state; do NOT rename existing jobs; if you add a job it must follow the docs-only skip pattern); (5) the LOADER (index.html template/JS): if `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` fails because the host serves .wasm with the wrong MIME type, fall back to fetching an ArrayBuffer and `WebAssembly.instantiate` (Emscripten supports this: verify how stage 2's shell does it and make it robust and test it in the node smoke by a mock fetch that returns the wrong content type); progress display during download using the manifest sizes; load failure messages; (6) OPTIONAL lazy asset pack: let the player fetch its asset pack (.data) asynchronously with progress (Emscripten's preload via `--preload-file` is already fetched before start: the improvement is progress reporting and a clear error path; do NOT introduce a custom pack format unless small and tested); (7) docs/web-build.html updated: the budgets, manifest, precompressed outputs, loader behaviour, hosting recipes, what still is not done (audio, physics, WebGPU, threads); update docs/testing.html CI paragraph. Native builds must be completely unchanged. Nothing builds locally; the Emscripten CI job is the test, expect fix rounds. Unverified items: everything needing a real browser (progress display, MIME fallback in a real browser, Content-Encoding hosting recipes).
acceptance: All 10 checks unchanged and green; native builds identical
size/speed packages are built in CI; .br/.gz siblings and manifest.json are produced; plain files still work
Size budgets are enforced by CI from one budget file; chosen numbers justified from measurement
The loader falls back when .wasm is served with the wrong MIME type (node smoke with a mock fetch) and shows progress/errors; docs updated
notes: Reviewer: budgets reference real measured numbers and the budget file is the single source, CI job names unchanged (any new job follows the docs-only skip), precompressed files do not replace the plain ones, manifest hashes correct, the MIME fallback path really exercised by the smoke test, native builds untouched, docs true. Unverified: real-browser behaviour.
